PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Placental tissue (chorionic villi)
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Fetal chromosome analysis requested

TEST PERFORMED
Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH)
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)

METHODOLOGY
Array CGH analysis was performed on uncultured placental DNA using oligonucleotide microarray technology. The GenArray XR4 platform was utilized, containing approximately 60,000 genome-wide probes providing comprehensive coverage across all chromosomes. DNA was extracted from placental tissue, labeled, and hybridized according to manufacturer's protocols. Data analysis was performed using proprietary software with reference to the GRCh37/hg19 human genome assembly.

QF-PCR analysis was performed in parallel to rapidly exclude common aneuploidies and triploidy. Multiplex PCR amplification of short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, 21, X, and Y was conducted.

RESULTS

ARRAY CGH RESULT:
arr(1-22)x2,(X,Y)x1

INTERPRETATION: Normal male chromosome complement

No clinically significant copy number variants detected
No imbalances >1Mb identified
No known pathogenic microdeletions or microduplications detected

QF-PCR RESULT:
Chromosome 13: Two alleles detected - Normal disomic pattern
Chromosome 18: Two alleles detected - Normal disomic pattern
Chromosome 21: Two alleles detected - Normal disomic pattern
Sex chromosomes: XY pattern confirmed
Triploidy: Excluded

CLINICAL INTERPRETATION
The array CGH analysis demonstrates a normal male chromosome complement with no detectable genomic imbalances. The resolution of this analysis excludes chromosomal imbalances greater than 1Mb and smaller fully penetrant pathogenic variants included in the array design. The QF-PCR results are concordant, confirming normal copy number for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21, and excluding triploidy.

These results are consistent with a chromosomally normal male fetus.

LIMITATIONS
1. Array CGH cannot detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements (translocations, inversions)
2. Low-level mosaicism (<20%) may not be detected
3. Point mutations and small insertions/deletions are not detected by this methodology
4. Uniparental disomy cannot be excluded
5. This test was performed on placental tissue; confined placental mosaicism cannot be excluded

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis is required for this sample based on current findings. Standard prenatal care and monitoring should continue as clinically indicated.

This report has been reviewed and electronically signed by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Director, Prenatal Cytogenetics Laboratory
Board Certified Clinical Cytogeneticist
